processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Casting ingot homogenized at 1100 °C for 2hr before hot forging.
Hot forged to 50% thickness reduction in the temperature range 1050-800 °C followed by air cooling to room temperature.
Hot forged samples soaked at 1100 °C for 2hr prior to hot rolling.
Hot rolled in the temperature range 1050-800 °C in two passes with reheating at 1100 °C for 5 min between passes; 50% thickness reduction in each pass.

processing_steps.temperature: from finish rolling temperature (~800) to room temperature
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Water quenching of the hot-rolled sample from the finish rolling temperature (~800 °C) converts part of the austenite into lenticular martensite; remaining austenite is untransformed austenite.
Surface machining up to 1 mm depth on both sides of the hot rolled sheet to remove the oxide layer; resulting sheet thickness 3 mm.

structures.overall_structure: Dual-phase δ-ferrite + austenite matrix with lenticular martensite formed by water quenching; dendritic structures completely eliminated by further soaking at higher temperature; grains of both phases elongated along the rolling direction. Remaining austenite after water quenching is termed untransformed austenite.

phases_present.morphology: elongated islands along the rolling direction in a darker α/γ matrix
elongated lens/ellipse shaped islands distributed in the matrix
lenticular shape; fine lenticular/needle relief with internal parallel striations typical of martensite laths

grain_structure.texture: Both phases elongated in the rolling direction due to rolling effect

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: subsize specimen, machined by wire EDM along the rolling direction
diamond Berkovich tip (B-T 50), tip radius 100 nm, tip angle 142.3°
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: indentation load 30 mN; loading/unloading rate 60 mN/min; dwell time 10 s

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Product of strength and elongation (PSE): HRQ (hot rolled & quenched) = 1.01 GPa% versus best annealed condition IA750_60 Min = 7.9 GPa%; HRQ also has highest YS/UTS but lowest TE (1.5±0.5 %).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Bruker D8 advanced X-ray diffractometer, Co-Kα (1.79Å) target, step size 0.02°, 2θ range 20°-120°
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Co-Kα radiation; Rietveld refinement for phase fractions
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification and determination of austenite volume fraction before and after tensile testing
characterization_methods.key_findings: Ferrite and austenite reflections in HRQ; HRQ austenite volume fraction ~19% before and ~18% after tensile test.

characterization_methods.technique: Optical microscopy (with differential interference contrast (DIC) insert)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Leica optical microscope; Villella's Reagent etching (5 ml HCl + 1 gm picric acid + 100 ml ethanol) for 10-15 s; colloidal polishing 0.25 µm
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructural examination of the HRQ specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: Shows elongated δ-ferrite islands along the rolling direction; DIC inset labels δ and α/γ; dendritic structures eliminated in HRQ.

characterization_methods.technique: Field Emission Gun Scanning Electron Microscopy (FEG-SEM)
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructural imaging of phases in the HRQ specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: δ in large featureless grey areas; α/γ grains show fine lenticular/needle relief and internal parallel striations typical of martensite laths.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS VP 300 SEM equipped with EDAX
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: At least 5-7 areas and 15-20 spots averaged with standard deviation
characterization_methods.purpose: Elemental analysis of individual phases in the HRQ specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: δ-ferrite Mn 7.02±0.25 wt.%, Al 5.61±0.11 wt.%; austenite/martensite Mn 8.36±0.16 wt.%, Al 4.75±0.11 wt.%; Mn enriched in austenite/martensite and Al in δ-ferrite.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEG-SEM (ZEISS VP 300) with EBSD camera, 20 kV, step size 0.5 µm; post-processing in TSL-OIM
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase mapping of the HRQ specimen (BCC vs FCC)
characterization_methods.key_findings: EBSD phase map superimposed on IQ map confirms green FCC (austenite) elongated islands in red BCC matrix, verifying retained/untransformed austenite and martensite formation.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Anton Paar (NHT1000038550), diamond Berkovich tip (B-T 50), tip radius 100 nm, tip angle 142.3°
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: loading/unloading rate 60 mN/min, dwell time 10 s, indentation load 30 mN
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure nano hardness of individual phases (δ-ferrite, untransformed austenite, martensite) in the HRQ specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: δ-ferrite 4439±206 MPa, untransformed austenite 4080±360 MPa, martensite 8897±550 MPa; load-displacement max penetration ~550 nm (untransformed austenite) and ~384 nm (martensite) at 30 mN.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, strain rate 2.67×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹, subsize specimens (ASTM E8/E8M) machined along rolling direction; at least three samples averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Evaluate mechanical properties of the HRQ specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: HRQ: YS 486±6 MPa, UTS 674±20 MPa, TE 1.5±0.5 %, PSE 1.01 GPa%.

characterization_methods.purpose: Examine fracture surface of the tensile-tested HRQ specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: HRQ fracture surface exhibits mainly cleavage and/or flat facets, representing brittle mode of failure.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium phase fraction vs temperature (200-1600 °C); identified duplex δ-ferrite + austenite region ~650-1350 °C
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Dilatometry test on hot forged sample showed no significant deviation, consistent with negligible transformation; 750 °C intercritical annealing temperature selected based on the duplex region.

computational_details.simulation_method: Thermodynamic SFE model proposed by Olson and Cohen
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Inputs include grain size (initially assumed 40 µm austenite), temperature and alloy composition; ΔG_chem=245.267 J/mole, ΔG_mag=0.0029319 J/mole, ΔG_ex=19.6842 J/mole, molar surface density ρ=2.9328×10⁻⁵ mol/m², interfacial surface energy 10 mJ/m²
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Theoretical SFE ~35 mJ/m² matches the 20-40 mJ/m² design window; for reverted austenite of IA750_60 Min (Mn 7.58 wt.%, Al 3.96 wt.%) recalculated SFE ~27 mJ/m².

analytical_models.equation_role: Compute stacking fault energy of austenite (γ_SFE = 2ρΔG^{γ→ε} + 2σ^{γ/ε})
analytical_models.model_note: Used to design the steel into the 20-40 mJ/m² SFE window (TWIP as major mechanism). For IA750_60 Min reverted austenite SFE recalculated to ~27 mJ/m²; a C change to ~0.05 wt.% changes SFE to ~2 mJ/m².

unmapped_findings: Martensite start (Ms) temperature of the HRQ condition calculated according to an empirical equation is ~350 °C, supporting the transformation of austenite to martensite due to water quenching (block b0038).

EDS of the HRQ specimen: Mn and Al concentration in δ-ferrite are 7.02±0.25 wt.% and 5.61±0.11 wt.%; in austenite/martensite they are 8.36±0.16 wt.% and 4.75±0.11 wt.%, showing Mn enrichment in austenite/martensite and Al enrichment in δ-ferrite (block b0038, figure_003).

HRQ austenite volume fraction: ~19% before tensile test and ~18% after tensile test; transformation ratio ~5.5%; mechanical stability parameter K ≈ 3.26 (3.216 in Fig. 7c), indicating very stable austenite due to C and Mn diffusion accelerated by δ-ferrite (blocks b0054, b0061, figure_007).
HRQ product of strength and elongation (PSE) = 1.01 GPa% (Hot Rolled row of Table 3), the lowest among all studied conditions (block b0057, table_003).
HRQ fracture surface exhibits mainly cleavage and/or flat facet type structure representing a brittle mode of failure due to the high fraction of δ-ferrite (block b0072, figure_011).
The stress-strain plastic region showed no serrations (no TWIP effect), consistent with the high SFE of these alloys (block b0073).

Nanoindentation load-displacement curves indicate a maximum penetration depth of ~550 nm for untransformed austenite versus ~384 nm for martensite under the same 30 mN load, confirming martensite is the harder phase (block b0044, table_002).

The HRQ specimen's higher YS (486±6 MPa) and UTS (674±20 MPa) with lowest TE (1.5±0.5 %) are attributed to the presence of hard martensite along with retained austenite and δ-ferrite in the microstructure (block b0046).
